subject: biology

hotspots.label: Rough ER
hotspots.description: The portion of the ER covered in ribosomes, where proteins are built and folded.
hotspots.function: Builds and folds proteins with the help of its ribosomes.

hotspots.label: Smooth ER
hotspots.description: The portion without ribosomes, which makes lipids and processes molecules.
hotspots.function: Makes fats and helps process and move molecules.

hotspots.label: Transport bubble (vesicle)
hotspots.description: A small membrane bubble that buds off the ER to carry materials to other organelles.
hotspots.function: Carries finished products to the next stop.

hotspots.label: Membrane network
hotspots.description: The connected maze of folded membranes that spreads through the cytoplasm.
hotspots.function: Provides the highway that moves materials around the cell.

assetBrief: SUBJECT: the endoplasmic reticulum as a connected folded membrane network shown in a cutaway cell slice. The membranes form many wavy, flattened sacs and tubes spreading through the frame. One region is studded with small ribosome dots (rough ER); a smoother region continues as tubes (smooth ER). A few small membrane bubbles (vesicles) are shown budding off at the edges, in the process of carrying cargo. Warm-paper muted palette, restrained. Named nodes: RoughER, SmoothER, RibosomeDots, Vesicle01-04. Budget 12-18k.
